rates.note: Six straight weekly increases; highest PMMS reading since November 2023. Daily trackers were 7.5%+ on Oct 7.

narrative:
Here is what changed in the last six weeks. Mortgage rates went from 6.65% in late August to 7.28% on October 1, the highest since November 2023, after the Fed's first hike since 2023 (to 3.75 to 4.00% on Sep 16) and a 10-year Treasury above 5% for the first time since 2007. A buyer who could reach $1,000,000 in July can now reach about $910,000 on the same payment. The buyer did not change their mind about your seller's house; the math changed.

The demand data confirms it. Purchase applications are down 14% year over year. Redfin's pending sales are at a near three-year low. Reports On Housing counts 3,296 pending sales in LA County over the last 30 days, the weakest September since it began tracking in 2012, while active inventory climbed to 15,003. Expected Market Time jumped from 129 to 137 days in two weeks, versus 114 a year ago. In Orange County, 43% of active listings have already cut price. Nationally, sellers outnumber buyers by 58%, the widest gap on record.

Yet closed-sale data still looks fine: LA County's August median was $922K, up 1.4%, with 37.6% selling above list at a 99.5% sale-to-list ratio. That is the trap. Those closings were negotiated in June and July at 6.4 to 6.5%. Expect September and October closings to show the strain. Two markets now exist: homes priced to today's buyer, which still draw multiple offers, especially under $750K and in the Inland Empire, and homes priced to spring, which sit.

For a listing at 60-plus days, the honest conversation is this: the home has been shown to the buyers who were looking, at a payment they could not make. A 5% price reduction roughly offsets the purchasing power lost since July. Waiting for rates to fall is a bet against a Fed that just signaled more hikes, into a season where listings thin out but buyers thin out faster. Prop 19 portability, equity (distressed sales in LA County: 247 all year) and strong rents give most sellers options; the one option that is closing is the price from May.

under750: Still the healthiest band: Victorville, Lancaster and Palmdale sell above list 46 to 53% of the time in 38 to 55 days (Aug 2026). Buyers here are the most rate sensitive: 0.5 point is $165 to $205 a month on a $600K to $750K purchase.
Price-drop shares in these cities run 32 to 37%, double LA County's 17%. A sub-$750K listing at 60+ days with no offers is almost always price or condition, not the market.
Yucca Valley is the exception: 77 DOM, 96.8% sale-to-list, 36.7% price drops. FAIR Plan insurance rises 29.1% on Oct 15. Get an insurance quote before relisting.
Condos: LA County condo Expected Market Time is 188 days versus 117 for detached. HOA dues plus insurance hit the payment-constrained buyer hardest.
750to1500: This is the county median (LA $922K to $947K, Ventura $867K to $925K). Buyers here lost roughly $80K to $130K of purchasing power since July on the same payment and usually have no cash cushion.
Ventura County shows the softest data of the four counties: sales down 11.9% year over year, median down 1.3%, 21.4% of listings with price drops. Do not use OC's appreciation as a reference.
OC under $1M moves in 45 days, so a stale OC condo or entry home is a pricing issue. 43% of OC actives have cut; median list ($1.725M SFR) sits far above median closed ($1.41M).

Script: The buyers who toured in August were qualified at 6.7%. The same buyers are qualified today for about 5% less house. We can meet them or wait for the next group, which the data says is smaller.
1500to3000: Jumbo rates are 7.27 to 7.66%, so the payment on a $2M home moved from about $10.4K to $10.9K in six weeks before taxes and a rising insurance bill. OC $2M+ takes 58 days versus 39 for $1M to $2M.
LA County's $2M+ segment has an Expected Market Time of 258 days, nearly twice the county average. Last year's band table showed $2M to $3M at 149 days and $3M to $4M at 222; expect worse now.
Cash buyers (27% of sales nationally) are the leverage. A cash-ready price beats a financed-buyer fantasy price.

Beverly Hills study: homes priced within 3% of value closed in 29 days at 99.1%; homes that needed a reduction averaged $342K below original list and 73 days. A stale listing here has usually already lost more than the reduction it resisted.
over3000: Discounts are the norm: 14% and 42% under-ask closings reported in Beverly Hills; Malibu absorption 12%. The 2025 band table had $4M to $8M at 309 days and $8M+ at 593.
Measure ULA still takes 4% at about $5M and 5.5% at about $10M inside LA city, a $200K to $550K haircut that Beverly Hills or Santa Monica comps do not carry.
The 10-year at 5.3% matters twice: jumbo rates and the opportunity cost of parking cash. Treasuries paying 5% risk-free compete with the house; the listing needs to be finished, private and turnkey.
Insurance is a closing risk: FAIR Plan premiums in high-fire zones may double on Oct 15 renewals. Get a bindable quote into the disclosure package.
Seller over 55 moving down: Prop 19 lets them carry the old tax base to any California replacement home up to three times, which often matters more than the last 3% of price.
